title: Hardship Skip Allowance and Assistance Recalculation Setting
content:
For patients whose circumstances change while they are on a plan, **Patient Payment Plans** terms carry two kinds of setting: a hardship skip allowance, and whether a reduction granted under the Patient Financial Assistance Program recomputes the installment.

| Term | Hardship skips allowed per plan | Supporting document required for a skip | Installment recomputed after an assistance adjustment |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3-Month Payment Plan | 0 | Yes | No |
| 6-Month Payment Plan | 0 | Yes | No |
| 9-Month Payment Plan | 0 | Yes | No |
| 12-Month Payment Plan | 1 | Yes | Yes |
| 18-Month Payment Plan | 1 | Yes | Yes |
| 24-Month Extended Payment Plan | 2 | Yes | Yes |

## What the settings mean

**Hardship skips allowed** is the number of installments that may be deferred to the end of the plan for a documented hardship; 0 means none. The 12-Month and 18-Month terms allow one skip and the 24-Month Extended Payment Plan allows two.

**Supporting document required** states whether a hardship skip needs a supporting document, such as a job-loss notice or a medical leave letter. Every term requires one.

**Installment recomputed after an assistance adjustment** states whether a financial-assistance reduction recomputes the installment. Where the setting is *No* (the 3-, 6- and 9-month terms), the installment stays as it is and the term shortens.

## Points of judgement

- A patient on the 9-Month Payment Plan has no hardship skip available, with or without documents.
- A patient on the 24-Month Extended Payment Plan who has used one skip still has one more, and only with a supporting document.
- An assistance reduction on a 6-Month Payment Plan leaves the installment unchanged; the plan simply ends sooner.
